advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether `--clean` should commit the removal of COMMITTED foreign paths, or explicitly report them as unpersisted rather than 'removed'.
evidence: ABSENCE: no `git commit` call anywhere in tracker_maintenance_cli after the foreign-path removal loop; the run ends at line 274 with `return 0`
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:457: `f" {len(committed)} of them are COMMITTED to the tickets branch ... will propagate on the next push."`
Output claims completion regardless: tracker_maintenance.py:272 `f"repaired: {len(stranded)} stranded, {len(foreign)} foreign path(s) removed"`
advisory.finding: When a foreign top-level path is COMMITTED to the tickets branch, `--clean` removes it from the worktree and unstages it with `git rm --cached ... --ignore-unmatch`, but never commits the removal, so the deletion is not persisted to the tickets branch even though the command prints 'repaired' and records the path in the audit line. fsck's own report distinguishes committed strays as 'strictly worse ... will propagate on the next push', yet the repair leaves them uncommitted (a dangling staged deletion) rather than actually removing them from history/the branch.
scenarios: A source tree (e.g. `src/`) was committed into the tickets branch; operator runs `--clean`; the worktree files are gone and audit says removed, but the commit removing them is never created so the pollution reappears / still propagates on the next push.

_USAGE: 'this is for a store that rebar itself cannot write.'

Users running `rebar tracker-maintenance --help` see a shorter text than what the docs promise.
merged_from: The in-module `_USAGE` string and the pinned help text disagree in wording ('a store that rebar itself cannot write' vs 'a store rebar itself cannot write'), producing two divergent authoritative help texts for the same command.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that seeds an unmerged (`--diff-filter=U`) index entry and asserts `--clean` restores a regenerable ticket path from HEAD, removes a stranded foreign path, and records it in the audit line's `stranded_paths`.
evidence: Fixture creates only untracked pollution: `(tracker / "src").mkdir()` / `(tracker / "src" / "leak.py").write_text(...)` (test file lines 54-56) — no unmerged index entry

Repair partition never reached with content: `regenerable = [p for p in stranded ...]` / `discard_unmerged_paths(tracker, regenerable, stranded_foreign)` (tracker_maintenance.py:239-241) — `stranded` is always empty
search of test file for 'stranded' returns (no matches); `test_clean...` asserts only `foreign_paths == ["src"]`, never a stranded path
docstring names this the exact state to repair: '_stranded_paths ... Paths left unmerged in the index (the state that blocks every ticket write)'
advisory.finding: The stranded/unmerged-index repair path — the core 'wedged store' scenario the command exists to fix — is never exercised. Every test uses a fixture that only creates an untracked foreign worktree tree (`src/leak.py`); `_stranded_paths` reads `git diff --diff-filter=U`, so `stranded` is `[]` in all six tests. `discard_unmerged_paths()` and the regenerable-vs-stranded_foreign partition (tracker_maintenance.py:239-241) are therefore never covered. A regression that restored a regenerable ticket path incorrectly, deleted one that HEAD still tracks, or left the index unmerged would pass the whole suite.
scenarios: A store wedged by an unmerged index (the incident that motivated the command) is repaired incorrectly and no test catches it
A regression restores/deletes the wrong side of the regenerable-vs-foreign partition for stranded paths

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the tracker-maintenance dispatch comment to reflect that ensure_initialized still auto-links/attaches (only first-time init is gated).
evidence: diff src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py: `# ... must never auto-init one — an operator reaching for maintenance is repairing an EXISTING store, and silently creating a fresh one would hide that.` then `ensure_initialized(init_only=False)`
src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:100-106: `pending_init_attaches_to_existing` path calls `init_core` automatically 'even with no TTY'
dropped.finding: The dispatch comment asserts tracker-maintenance 'must never auto-init one', but `ensure_initialized(init_only=False)` auto-creates a tracker in the symlink and attach-to-existing-branch cases even without a TTY (via `_create_tracker`), contradicting the comment's stated intent.
scenarios: Reader trusts the comment and assumes maintenance never materializes a tracker; in a linked-worktree/attach scenario it silently does.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Parse `git diff --name-only` output with `.splitlines()` instead of `.split()` in `_stranded_paths`.
dropped.finding: `_stranded_paths` splits `git diff --name-only` output with `res.stdout.split()` (whitespace), which corrupts paths containing spaces and can silently mis-parse git's quoted/escaped path output; use `.splitlines()` (and account for core.quotePath).
scenarios: A stranded/unmerged path containing a space is split into multiple bogus tokens, so the repair operates on non-existent paths and misses the real one.
